tasks.title: Request counter in state
tasks.statement:
GET /hit replies «хит N», where N is the sequence number of the request. The counter lives in the state: Arc<AtomicUsize> (Ordering::SeqCst). main sends three requests.

Expected output:
```
хит 1
хит 2
хит 3
```
tasks.hint: State(c): State<Arc<AtomicUsize>>; fetch_add(1) + 1; for the router: .with_state(Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0))).

tasks.title: Log in a Mutex
tasks.statement:
POST /log/{msg} appends msg to a shared list, GET /log returns all entries separated by commas in the order they were added. State: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> (std::sync::Mutex; the lock must not live across an await; there is no await here).

Expected output:
```
201 Created
201 Created
201 Created
один,два,три
```
tasks.hint: lock().unwrap().push(..); join(",").

tasks.title: Config in an RwLock
tasks.statement:
The state is Arc<RwLock<String>> with a greeting (initially «привет»). GET /greet returns the greeting, PUT /greet/{text} replaces it and replies 204. Check before and after the replacement.

Expected output:
```
привет
204 No Content
здравствуйте
```
tasks.hint: std::sync::RwLock: read().unwrap().clone(); write().unwrap().

tasks.title: Lock across an await
tasks.statement:
The handler GET /add/{n} takes a Tokio mutex (tokio::sync::Mutex<Vec<u32>>), adds n, waits 5 ms (sleep) WHILE HOLDING the lock and replies with the sum of all numbers in the list at that moment. Five requests arrive at once (join_all); the sums must be strictly sequential: each request sees the result of the previous one. Print the sorted responses.

Expected output:
```
5
максимум: 15
все различны: true
```
tasks.hint: tokio::sync::Mutex: let mut g = m.lock().await; push; sleep.await; sum.

tasks.title: Part of the state via FromRef
tasks.statement:
AppState contains config: Config { name: String } and hits: Arc<AtomicUsize>. Implement FromRef<AppState> for Config and for Arc<AtomicUsize>. The handler GET /name takes only State<Config> and replies with the name, GET /hit takes only State<Arc<AtomicUsize>> and replies with the number of hits after incrementing.

Expected output:
```
чат
1
2
```
tasks.hint: impl FromRef<AppState> for Config { fn from_ref(s: &AppState) -> Config { s.config.clone() } }

tasks.title: Two routers with different state
tasks.statement:
Router a() uses state String («A»), router b() uses u32 (42). Each calls .with_state(..) on itself, which gives a Router<()>. Combine them in app() with the merge method. GET /a replies «a=A», GET /b replies «b=42».

Expected output:
```
a=A
b=42
```
tasks.hint: with_state turns Router<S> into Router<()>; merging two Router<()> is allowed.

tasks.title: Extension from middleware
tasks.statement:
A layer (from_fn) reads the x-user header: if it is present and is a number, it puts UserId(n) into the request extensions, otherwise it replies 401 without calling the handler. GET /me replies «вы: N». Check requests with the header, with a non-numeric one, and without it.

Expected output:
```
(200, "вы: 7")
(401, "")
(401, "")
```
tasks.hint: req.extensions_mut().insert(UserId(n)); handler: Extension(UserId(n)): Extension<UserId>.

tasks.title: A layer adds a header
tasks.statement:
Write a from_fn middleware that, after processing, adds the header x-done: yes to the response. The route GET /a replies «a». Print the header for /a and for the unknown path /zzz (a layer attached with .layer covers the 404 too).

Expected output:
```
Some("yes")
Some("yes")
```
tasks.hint: res.headers_mut().insert("x-done", HeaderValue::from_static("yes")).

tasks.title: Layer order: Router::layer
tasks.statement:
Two from_fn_with_state layers with a shared log (Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>) are attached to the route GET /x: «outer» and «inner». Each layer writes «name-in» before calling next and «name-out» after; the handler writes «handler». Attach the layers with the .layer method so that the order of entries is: outer-in inner-in handler inner-out outer-out. Write the layer function tag and the assembly.

Expected output:
```
200 OK
outer-in inner-in handler inner-out outer-out
```
tasks.hint: The last .layer is the outermost: first .layer(inner), then .layer(outer).

tasks.title: route_layer and unknown paths
tasks.statement:
A layer adds the header x-seen: 1. Attach it so that the header is present on responses of existing routes (/ok) but NOT on the response for an unknown path (/zzz). main prints whether the header is present for both.

Expected output:
```
/ok: true
/zzz: false
```
tasks.hint: Use .route_layer(..) instead of .layer(..).

tasks.title: Authorization with a layer
tasks.statement:
A layer checks the header Authorization: Bearer secret. No header or a different token: 401 and the body «нужен токен». Attach the layer only to GET /private (route_layer on a separate router), while GET /public must reply without the check. Print the status and body for three requests.

Expected output:
```
(200, "открыто")
(401, "нужен токен")
(200, "секрет")
```
tasks.hint: Router::new().route("/private", ..).route_layer(from_fn(auth)).route("/public", ..): the layer applies to the routes added before it.

tasks.title: Statistics by path
tasks.statement:
A layer counts requests per path: the state is Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, u32>>>. The layer works on from_fn_with_state and increments the path counter before calling next. GET /stats replies «path=count» separated by commas, with paths in alphabetical order (/stats itself is counted too, before the response is built).

Expected output:
```
/a=3,/b=1,/stats=1
```
tasks.hint: HashMap::entry(path).or_default() += 1; sort the keys in /stats.

tasks.title: map_request: modify the request
tasks.statement:
Using middleware::map_request, convert the value of the x-name header to upper case before the handler. The handler GET /hello replies «привет, ИМЯ» (the name is the header value). If the header is missing: «привет, незнакомец».

Expected output:
```
привет, ANNA
привет, незнакомец
```
tasks.hint: map_request(|mut req: Request| async move { ...; req }); to_uppercase.

tasks.title: map_response: modify the response
tasks.statement:
Using middleware::map_response, add the header x-powered-by: say to all responses. Print the header value for the 200 response (/a) and for the 404 (/zzz).

Expected output:
```
(200, Some("say"))
(404, Some("say"))
```
tasks.hint: map_response(|mut res: Response| async move { ...; res }); .layer(..) covers the 404 too.

tasks.title: Request identifier
tasks.statement:
A layer assigns each request an identifier «req-N» (N is the sequence number, the counter is in the state Arc<AtomicUsize>, starting from 1), puts it into the request extensions as RequestId(String) and into the response header x-request-id. The handler GET /id replies with the same identifier taken from the extension. Print the body and the header for two requests.

Expected output:
```
("req-1", Some("req-1"))
("req-2", Some("req-2"))
```
tasks.hint: Extension<RequestId> in the handler; res.headers_mut().insert("x-request-id", ..).

tasks.title: Processing time in a header
tasks.statement:
A layer measures the request processing time (Instant) and adds the header x-elapsed-ms with an integer number of milliseconds. The handler GET /slow sleeps 30 ms. main prints whether the number in the header is at least 30 and less than 1000.

Expected output:
```
true
```
tasks.hint: let t = Instant::now(); let mut res = next.run(req).await; ... t.elapsed().as_millis().

tasks.title: TimeoutLayer: 408
tasks.statement:
Attach tower_http::timeout::TimeoutLayer with a limit of 50 ms and status code 408 Request Timeout. The handler /slow sleeps 300 ms, /fast replies immediately. Print the statuses.

Expected output:
```
200 OK
408 Request Timeout
```
tasks.hint: TimeoutLayer::with_status_code(StatusCode::REQUEST_TIMEOUT, Duration::from_millis(50)).

tasks.title: Body size limit: 413
tasks.statement:
Attach tower_http::limit::RequestBodyLimitLayer with 10 bytes. POST /echo (the handler takes the body as a String and returns it) must reply 413 for a body longer than the limit and echo a short one. Print the results for bodies of 5 and 50 characters (ASCII).

Expected output:
```
(200, "aaaaa")
413 Payload Too Large
```
tasks.hint: RequestBodyLimitLayer::new(10); the String extractor reads the whole body.

tasks.title: Concurrency limit
tasks.statement:
Attach tower::limit::ConcurrencyLimitLayer with 2. The handler GET /w increments the active counter (AtomicUsize), records the maximum, sleeps 20 ms and decrements. Five requests arrive at once. Print the maximum number of simultaneous handlers.

Expected output:
```
true
максимум: 2
```
tasks.hint: ConcurrencyLimitLayer::new(2); the maximum via fetch_max.

tasks.title: CORS headers
tasks.statement:
Attach tower_http::cors::CorsLayer::permissive(). A GET /a request with the header Origin: http://example.com must get access-control-allow-origin in the response. Print the header value.

Expected output:
```
Some("*")
```
tasks.hint: CorsLayer::permissive() allows any origin.

tasks.title: ServiceBuilder: order from top to bottom
tasks.statement:
Assemble two layers (from_fn_with_state with a shared log) with tower::ServiceBuilder: «first» first, «second» second. The order of entries must be: first-in second-in handler second-out first-out. Hint: in ServiceBuilder the layer listed first is the outermost.

Expected output:
```
200 OK
first-in second-in handler second-out first-out
```
tasks.hint: Router::new().route(..).layer(ServiceBuilder::new().layer(first).layer(second)).

tasks.title: A custom Layer and Service
tasks.statement:
Implement by hand the layer CountLayer(Arc<AtomicUsize>) and the service Count<S>: each call of the service increments the counter and passes the request inward. For this you need impl<S> Layer<S> for CountLayer and impl<S> Service<Request<Body>> for Count<S> with poll_ready (delegates to the inner one) and call (clones the counter, calls the inner service and returns its future in Box::pin). Attach the layer with the .layer(CountLayer(..)) method; main sends 4 requests and prints the counter value.

Expected output:
```
4
```
tasks.hint: type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<S::Response, S::Error>> + Send>>; do not forget to clone the service in call via std::mem::replace.

tasks.title: Token bucket
tasks.statement:
Implement the struct Bucket { capacity, per_sec } with the method allow(now_ms: u64) -> bool. The bucket is initially full (capacity tokens) and refills at per_sec tokens per second (fractional tokens accumulate, and it never grows above capacity). allow spends one token if there is one (>= 1) and returns true; otherwise false. Time is monotonically non-decreasing. Pure logic: the time comes in as a parameter.

Expected output:
```
[true, true, true, false, false, true, false, true, false, true, true, true, false]
```
tasks.hint: Keep tokens: f64 and last_ms; before the check add (now - last)/1000 * per_sec and clamp to capacity.

tasks.title: Broadcast channel in the state
tasks.statement:
The state contains a broadcast::Sender<String>. POST /say/{text} publishes text and replies with the number of receivers it was delivered to (the result of send; 0 if there are no subscribers, in which case send returns an error). main subscribes twice, sends a message, prints the response and what each subscriber received; then it drops all subscribers and sends once more.

Expected output:
```
доставлено: 2
привет
привет
доставлено: 0
```
tasks.hint: tx.send(text).unwrap_or(0); subscribers receive via rx.recv().await.

tasks.title: Room registry
tasks.statement:
State: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>>> (room → members). POST /rooms/{room}/join/{user} adds a member (creating the room), GET /rooms/{room}/members returns the members separated by commas in alphabetical order, and for a nonexistent room: 404 and the text «нет комнаты».

Expected output:
```
(200, "аня,вера")
(200, "борис")
(404, "нет комнаты")
```
tasks.hint: BTreeSet gives alphabetical order; entry().or_default().insert.

tasks.title: Fix: with_state was forgotten
tasks.statement:
The code does not compile: the router turned out to be of type Router<Arc<AtomicUsize>>, but app() must return Router<()>. Add the missing call so that GET /n replies «0», then «1».

Expected output:
```
0
1
```
tasks.hint: Router::with_state(Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0))).

tasks.title: Fix: the auth layer hides the log
tasks.statement:
There are two layers: «log» writes the response status to the log, «auth» replies 401 to requests without the x-token header. Right now the 401 record does not get into the log, because log ended up inside auth. Change the order of attaching so that the log sees the 401 as well. main prints the log after a request without a token and after a request with a token.

Expected output:
```
401,200
```
tasks.hint: The layer added last is the outermost: log must come after auth.

tasks.title: Config in an Arc
tasks.statement:
Config { name: String, max_users: u32 } is stored in the state as Arc<Config>. GET /config replies «имя: NAME, лимит: N». GET /admit/{n}: if n is not greater than max_users, «принят», otherwise 429 and «лимит исчерпан».

Expected output:
```
имя: чат, лимит: 100
(200, "принят")
(429, "лимит исчерпан")
```
tasks.hint: State(cfg): State<Arc<Config>>; a tuple response for the 429.

tasks.title: A missing extension
tasks.statement:
The handler GET /me requires Extension<UserId>, but the layer that puts it in is attached only to /secure/me. Print the status of GET /secure/me and GET /me: when the extension is missing, axum replies 500 and the handler is not called. The layer puts UserId(1) in without any checks.

Expected output:
```
(200, "пользователь 1")
500 Internal Server Error
```
tasks.hint: route_layer on a separate route; Extension<UserId> without the layer gives 500.

tasks.title: Own timeout in from_fn
tasks.statement:
Write a from_fn layer that limits processing to 30 ms via tokio::time::timeout: if the time runs out, reply 504 and «шлюз: таймаут», otherwise the normal response. GET /slow sleeps 200 ms, GET /fast replies immediately. Print the statuses and bodies.

Expected output:
```
(200, "быстро")
(504, "шлюз: таймаут")
```
tasks.hint: match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(30), next.run(req)).await { Ok(r) => r, Err(_) => ... }
